description: I am participating solo to build ASTRA CARE, an educational software prototype for monitoring simulated astronaut health indicators during long-duration space missions. It tracks heart rate, sleep duration, stress level, and oxygen reading, highlights simulated readings outside demo ranges with non-medical alerts, visualizes trends over time, and allows exporting history as CSV. It is a student prototype and not a medical device.
summary: ASTRA CARE is a browser-based astronaut health monitoring and bio-telemetry dashboard designed for long-duration space missions. During extended orbital and deep-space flights, crews face radiation, isolation, microgravity, and confined environments that can affect cardiovascular, immune, musculoskeletal, and psychological health. We developed an interactive HTML/JavaScript monitoring prototype deployed on Google Sites that tracks crew biometrics and simulates mission scenarios such as normal mission operations, elevated heart rate/exertion, low SpO2/cabin pressure drops, and solar radiation spikes. Real-time status indicators and recommended actions help crew members and support teams quickly recognize anomalies and respond to health changes. This matters because accessible, visual telemetry tools support crew self-monitoring and situational awareness when immediate Earth-based medical intervention may be delayed.
details:
How It Works & Key Features: ASTRA CARE is an interactive web biotelemetry dashboard built as a self-contained HTML/JavaScript application and hosted on Google Sites. Users can switch between crew profiles (such as Cmdr. Elena Vance) and trigger simulation presets—including Normal Mission, High Heart Rate / Exertion, Low SpO2 / Cabin Pressure Drop, and Solar Radiation Spike—to observe live telemetry updates, system status banners, and recommended crew actions.

Benefits & Impact: By presenting physiological trends and critical alerts in a clear visual interface, ASTRA CARE helps astronauts and mission operators monitor health shifts early and take timely corrective steps during long-duration missions.

Tools, Languages & Technologies: Developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for instant browser execution with zero heavy local dependencies, and published via Google Sites for public web access.

Creativity & Design Considerations: We focused on clarity under stress, rapid scenario testing, and zero-setup browser accessibility so anyone can inspect and interact with the prototype immediately.
